Risk capital is the capital cushion that the firm must set aside to cover worst-case loss scenarios less expected loss for credit, market, operational, business and reputation risk as defined by the targeted confidence interval. The time horizon for this measure is generally one year but it can span any time period.

Strategic capital is the capital cushion set aside to cover significant investments where success and profitability have a great degree of uncertainty. It is the sum of goodwill and burned out capital. The time horizon for this measure is generally one year but it can span any time period.

Economic capital is the capital cushion set aside to cover all risk that the enterprise is facing in addition to expected losses. It is the sum of risk capital (credit, market, operational, business and reputation risks) and strategic capital. The time horizon for this measure is generally one year but it can span any time period.

Strategic capital is the capital cushion set aside to cover significant investments where success and profitability have a great degree of uncertainty. It is the sum of goodwill and burned out capital. The time horizon for this measure is generally one year but it can span any time period. This granularity is at the product group/portfolio level.

Risk capital is the capital cushion that the firm must set aside to cover worst-case loss scenarios less expected loss for credit, market, operational, business and reputation risk as defined by the targeted confidence interval. Z-bonds are tranches where the bond coupon is accrued by adding the interest to the face value of the bond. The interest that normally would be paid to the parent bond during the lockout period is deferred and added to the Z-bond's principal value in a process called accretion.
